title: Meter Bridge
subject: electrical
aim: To find the resistance of a given wire using a meter bridge (Wheatstone bridge principle).
theory:
A meter bridge is a Wheatstone bridge whose ratio arms are the two segments of a uniform 100 cm wire. At the null point (zero galvanometer deflection) at length $l$ from the left end:

$$\frac{R}{X} = \frac{l}{100 - l} \Rightarrow X = R\,\frac{100 - l}{l}$$

The bridge is most sensitive when the null point is near the middle of the wire.
procedure: Connect the resistance box in the left gap and the unknown wire in the right gap.
Take out a resistance R from the box.
Slide the jockey along the wire to find the null point; note l.
Repeat for different values of R.
Calculate X for each reading and take the mean.
precautions: Press the jockey gently; do not slide it while pressing.
Choose R so that the null point is between 30 cm and 70 cm.

viva.question: Why is the null point method accurate?
viva.answer: At balance no current flows through the galvanometer, so its resistance does not affect the result.

viva.question: What are end errors?
viva.answer: Errors from the resistance of the copper strips and imperfect contacts at the ends of the wire.

viva.question: Why is the wire made of manganin or constantan?
viva.answer: They have a high resistivity and a low temperature coefficient of resistance.
